mechanism_claims.claim_text: Cec4-derived peptides, with C18 emphasized, directly altered S. aureus MW2 membrane potential at 32 µg/mL in a DiSC3(5) assay.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C13, C16, C18, C22; C18 highlighted as lead peptide
mechanism_claims.limitations: Assay supports membrane-potential disruption under tested in vitro conditions; it does not alone prove a single exclusive killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C18 and comparator derivatives increased propidium iodide uptake, liposome dye leakage, and Laurdan membrane-fluidity signal, supporting membrane permeabilization/disruption.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C13, C16, C18, C22; C18 at 32 µg/mL in figure/prose
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure/prose support the qualitative mechanism class and tested dose; exact graph values are not transcribed in local text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C18 killed S. aureus MW2 persisters in a time-kill assay; abstract reports 99% elimination at 10x MIC within 20 min.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C18 against S. aureus MW2 persisters
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is a functional killing result, not a distinct molecular target assignment.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C18 bound plasmid DNA in a band-shift assay; local text reports strong binding at 7.8 µM.
mechanism_claims.limitations: DNA binding is source-supported; the artifact preserves it alongside membrane effects rather than promoting it to the sole mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C18 reduced S. aureus MW2 biofilm attachment/formation and down-regulated virulence genes including agrA, fnb-A, and clf-1 in qPCR.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm and qPCR findings are functional/phenotypic context; they are not classified as a direct membrane mechanism.
